lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.13 - A Listen, point, and say

details: Listen, point, and say checks understanding of word meaning and sound. Listen and point shows students can match what they hear to the right image. Say practises first-step pronunciation.
Look for careful listening, correct pointing, clear sounds, and confident repetition.

“(singing) Happy birthday to me, happy birthday to me…Oh, guess what special day it is today? That’s right! It’s my birthday - it’s the Xth of xxx. What months are your birthdays in? Can you find the month  on the board?”

Heads Up: 
Focus the students’ attention on the CPT and present relevant features of the language (MFP). Then demonstrate the activity with TA/students.
Heads Down: 
Ss open their books. Instruct and ask ICQs. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Heads Together: 
Demo/Instruct and ask ICQs, including setting behaviour expectations. Then monitor, providing support and stretch where needed. Conduct activity feedback and error correction.
Reward moment
Check behaviour expectations and reward with APOS or remind for 4Rs

details: Listen and circle continues checking sound–image connection. Students practise listening for specific information and clearly circling an image.
Look for careful listening, accurate choices, pencil grip, and penmanship.
“I can’t remember Amy’s birthday! When is it? Can you help me? Let’s listen and find out”

lessonPlan.topic: Activity Book p.67 - B Circle and write

details: Circle and write gives students controlled practice spelling the sight words they locate. It reinforces whole-word memory, letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for correct spelling, consistent letter formation, and neat handwriting within the lines.
“I’m not going to be able to remember your birthdays unless I can spell all the months. Please write them out so I can make a proper list.”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - C. Ask and answer

details: Ask and answer gives students controlled practice using the target language to ask and respond to simple questions.
Look for the correct response to ‘What’s the date today?’ and clear and accurate responses.
“Ok, we know what months your birthdays are in. But what are the exact dates? Can you show me how to ask and answer to find out the date?”

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p.14 - D. Ask and answer. Then write.

details:
Ask and answer provides the opportunity to use the target structures with personalised information.
Write reinforces whole-word memory, letter order, and neat handwriting.
Look for accurate use of ‘When is your birthday’ and ‘It’s on the X of X’ with appropriate ordinal numbers and months, correct pronunciation, and natural turn-taking with classmates.
“Let’s find out exactly when our friends’ birthdays are by asking each other. Write them down so we can remember them and complete our class birthday list”.
